RU-A1-01-001.notes: брат ends in a consonant, so it's masculine and takes мой. The possessive agrees with the thing owned, not the owner: a woman also says мой брат.

RU-A1-01-002.notes: сестра ends in -а, so it's feminine and takes моя. Masculine nouns in -а (папа, дедушка) are the exception, because meaning beats form.

RU-A1-01-003.notes: письмо ends in -о, so it's neuter: моё. The neuter -ё is always stressed in моё, твоё, своё, and the dots are often left out in print (мое).

RU-A1-01-004.notes: квартира is feminine (-а), so наш becomes наша. наш and ваш have the same endings as мой: наш, наша, наше, наши.

RU-A1-01-005.notes: паспорт is masculine, and the cue вы gives ваш (your, polite or plural). ваш is capitalised (Ваш) in letters addressed to one person.

RU-A1-01-006.notes: словарь ends in -ь, which can be either gender; this one is masculine, so мой. The -ь nouns have to be learned with their gender: словарь m., тетрадь f.

RU-A1-01-007.notes: тетрадь is a feminine -ь noun, so the familiar 'your' is твоя. Most -ь nouns ending in -сть, -ть after a consonant, or -чь / -шь are feminine.

RU-A1-01-008.notes: его (his) never agrees: его машина, его дом, его письмо. It's a frozen genitive of он, which is why it doesn't change for the thing owned.

RU-A1-01-009.notes: её (her) is invariable like его, even though дом is masculine. Don't confuse it with the agreeing possessive: её дом, never ейный (dialect).

RU-A1-01-010.notes: папа ends in -а but denotes a man, so both the possessive and the past verb are masculine: мой папа пришёл. Gender follows meaning for such nouns.

RU-A1-01-011.notes: дедушка is masculine despite its -а ending, so наш, not наша. The same goes for дядя, мужчина and nicknames such as Саша for a man.

RU-A1-01-012.notes: Two -ь nouns side by side: словарь is masculine (мой), тетрадь feminine (моя). Nothing in the ending tells you; each has to be learned.

RU-A1-01-013.notes: очки exists only in the plural, so the possessive is plural: мои. 'One pair of glasses' is одни очки, not одно очко.

RU-A1-01-014.notes: часы (a watch or clock) is plural-only, so the verb is plural too: стоят. Here стоить means 'cost'; стоят дорого = are expensive.

RU-A1-01-015.notes: брюки is plural-only, so the adjective takes the plural -ые: новые брюки. Likewise джинсы, ножницы and деньги.

RU-A1-01-016.notes: телефон is masculine, so 'whose' is чей. Like мой, чей agrees with the thing owned: чей, чья, чьё, чьи.

RU-A1-01-017.notes: сумка is feminine, so чья. The word order Чья это сумка? keeps это invariable as the subject, and чья agrees with сумка.

RU-A1-01-018.notes: ключи is plural, so чьи. Note that это stays singular even with a plural noun: Чьи это ключи? The same holds for Это мои ключи, where это never becomes эти.

RU-A1-01-019.notes: друг has an irregular plural, друзья, with a г → з change and a soft -ья ending. The genitive plural is друзей.

RU-A1-01-020.notes: книга is feminine and its stem ends in г, so the spelling rule gives -и, not -ы: книги. The rule applies after г, к, х, ж, ш, щ, ч.

RU-A1-01-021.notes: студент ends in a hard consonant, so the plural is -ы: студенты. A female student is студентка (plural студентки).

RU-A1-01-022.notes: окно is neuter in -о, so the plural is -а: окна. The stress shifts in the plural, from окнó to óкна, as with many neuters.

RU-A1-01-023.notes: брат has the irregular plural братья (soft -ья). The verb живут is plural because the subject is plural.

RU-A1-01-024.notes: человек has a suppletive plural: люди. After numbers it reverts to человек: пять человек, never пять людей.

RU-A1-01-025.notes: ребёнок has the suppletive plural дети. The singular-sounding ребята is a different, colloquial word for 'guys, kids'.

RU-A1-01-026.notes: дом takes a stressed -а in the plural: домá, not домы. The same pattern gives города, поезда, учителя.

RU-A1-01-027.notes: карандаш ends in ш, so the spelling rule gives -и: карандаши. The stress falls on the ending throughout the plural.

RU-A1-01-028.notes: ключ ends in ч, so the plural is spelt ключи, never ключы. ключи от + genitive = the keys to something.
RU-A1-01-028.text: У тебя есть {{c1::ключи::ключ · plural}} от машины?
RU-A1-01-028.tr: Have you got the car keys?
RU-A1-01-028.flag: dup: replaced Где мои ключи? (near-identical to B2 Где же мои ключи?)

RU-A1-01-029.notes: Both words obey the spelling rule: хороший (ш) → хорошие, врач (ч) → врачи. Writing ы after these consonants is always wrong.

RU-A1-01-030.notes: вечер is masculine, and тихий has a stem in х, so the ending is -ий, not -ый. The same rule gives русский, лёгкий, долгий.

RU-A1-02-001.notes: машина is feminine, so новый becomes новая. Adjectives agree with their noun in gender, number and case.

RU-A1-02-002.notes: книга is feminine, so хорошая. The stem ends in ш, but the feminine ending is still -ая; the spelling rule only affects ы / и.

RU-A1-02-003.notes: кафе is an indeclinable loanword and is neuter, so новое. Indeclinable nouns in -е and -о are almost all neuter.

RU-A1-02-004.notes: слова is plural, and русский has a к stem, so the plural ending is -ие: русские. Nationality adjectives are written lower-case.

RU-A1-02-005.notes: море is neuter, and синий is a soft adjective, so -ее, not -ое. Soft adjectives keep the soft vowel in every ending: синяя, синие.

RU-A1-02-006.notes: семья is feminine, so большой becomes большая. Adjectives with stressed endings (большой, молодой) have -ой in the masculine but the usual -ая / -ое / -ие elsewhere.
RU-A1-02-006.flag: dup: replaced Это большая квартира (flagged against Это наша квартира)

RU-A1-02-007.notes: девушка is feminine, so красивая, and какая agrees too. Какая + adjective + noun! is the standard exclamation: what a…!

RU-A1-02-008.notes: платье is neuter, and летний is soft, so -ее: летнее. Season and time adjectives (зимний, вечерний, последний) are mostly soft.

RU-A1-02-009.notes: человек is masculine, and молодой has a stressed ending, so it ends in -ой, not -ый. Stress decides: новый (stem-stressed) but молодой, большой, плохой.

RU-A1-02-010.notes: машина is feminine, so какая. The question word agrees with the noun it asks about, exactly like an adjective.

RU-A1-02-011.notes: книги is plural, so какие, in an indirect question after знаешь. No change of word order is needed in the embedded question.

RU-A1-02-012.notes: Это on its own introduces something (this is…) and never changes; этот before a noun means 'this' and agrees with it: этот дом, эта улица. Here дом is masculine.

RU-A1-02-013.notes: улица is feminine, so этот becomes эта. Here the demonstrative modifies a noun, so it agrees; contrast Это улица (this is a street).
RU-A1-02-013.flag: dup: replaced Мне нравится эта песня (near-identical to A1 Мне нравится эта музыка); answer эта → Эта (sentence-initial)

RU-A1-02-014.notes: книги is plural, so эти. The predicate новые is a separate adjective; without эти, Это книги новые would be odd.

RU-A1-02-015.notes: Это introduces the noun phrase (these are…), so it stays это even with a plural: Это мои родители. Эти would need a predicate after it.

RU-A1-02-016.notes: кофе is masculine in the standard language, so чёрный. Neuter agreement (чёрное кофе) is now listed in dictionaries as colloquial, but it's still marked.

RU-A1-02-017.notes: пальто is an indeclinable neuter loanword, so моё. It never changes for case or number: в пальто, без пальто, два пальто. The form пальта is a recognised error.

RU-A1-02-018.notes: такси is indeclinable and neuter, so этот takes the neuter prepositional этом while такси itself stays put. на такси means 'by taxi'.
RU-A1-02-018.tip: такси never changes: в такси, на такси, без такси.

RU-A1-02-019.notes: этаже is prepositional after на, so the ordinal follows: третьем. третий is irregular, with a soft stem plus ь: третья, третье, третьего.

RU-A1-02-020.notes: поездка is feminine, so первая. Ordinals decline exactly like regular adjectives; only третий is irregular.

RU-A1-02-021.notes: With говорить the language is an adverb: по-русски (in Russian). With изучать, a transitive verb, it's the adjective + noun: русский язык.

RU-A1-03-001.notes: я + a first-conjugation verb in -ать takes -ю: читаю. The stem keeps its а: чита-ю, чита-ешь, чита-ют.

RU-A1-03-002.notes: ты takes -ешь: знаешь. In the present Russian doesn't distinguish 'do you know' and 'are you knowing'; one form covers both.

RU-A1-03-003.notes: она (third person) takes -ет: работает. в банке is the prepositional of place. The он, она and оно forms are identical in the present, so only the pronoun shows the gender.

RU-A1-03-004.notes: мы takes -ем: гуляем. гулять covers both a leisurely walk and going out to play; there's no separate verb for 'go for a walk'.

RU-A1-03-005.notes: вы takes -ете: понимаете. понимать по-русски uses the adverb, just like говорить по-русски. With a noun object it's понимать русский язык, which is less common in speech.

RU-A1-03-006.notes: они takes -ют after a vowel stem: слушают. слушать takes a direct object in the accusative: слушать музыку.

RU-A1-03-007.notes: говорить is second conjugation (-ить), so я takes -ю: говорю. The ты form is говоришь, with -и- in the endings.

RU-A1-03-008.notes: ты with a second-conjugation verb takes -ишь: говоришь. Second-conjugation verbs mostly end in -ить in the infinitive.

RU-A1-03-009.notes: он with звонить takes -ит: звонит. The stress is on the ending (звони́т); звóнит is a common but non-standard pronunciation.
RU-A1-03-009.tip: Standard stress is звони́т, not звóнит.

RU-A1-03-010.notes: смотреть is second conjugation despite -еть, so мы takes -им: смотрим. Other -еть verbs of this type: видеть, сидеть, терпеть.

RU-A1-03-011.notes: они with a second-conjugation verb takes -ят: говорят. The first-conjugation counterpart would be -ют.

RU-A1-03-012.notes: слышать has a stem in ш, so the spelling rule gives -у, not -ю: слышу. Russian uses the plain present for 'I can hear'.

RU-A1-03-013.notes: жить inserts -в- in the present: живу, живёшь. The endings are stressed, so ё appears in живёшь, живёт, живём, живёте.
RU-A1-03-013.tr: I live not far from work.
RU-A1-03-013.flag: dup: replaced Я живу в Москве (also in A1-05-001 and A1-06-021)

RU-A1-03-014.notes: ты takes the stressed ending -ёшь: живёшь. With a question like далеко от, Russian keeps the order of a statement and relies on intonation.
RU-A1-03-014.tr: Do you live far from the underground?
RU-A1-03-014.flag: dup: replaced Где ты живёшь? (repeated inside A1-06-020)

RU-A1-03-015.notes: писать changes с → ш in every present form: пишу, пишешь, пишут. The stress moves back after the я form: пишý but пи́шешь.
RU-A1-03-015.tr: I make mistakes when I write in Russian.
RU-A1-03-015.flag: dup: replaced Я пишу письмо (near-identical to A1-08-010)

RU-A1-03-016.notes: любить adds л in the я form only: люблю, but любишь. This л-insertion happens after б, п, в, ф, м in second-conjugation verbs.

RU-A1-03-017.notes: хотеть is mixed: singular forms are first conjugation with т → ч (хочу, хочешь, хочет), plural forms second conjugation (хотим, хотите, хотят).

RU-A1-03-018.notes: мы switches хотеть to the second-conjugation pattern: хотим. хочем is a common error and non-standard.
RU-A1-03-018.tip: хочем is non-standard; the мы form is хотим.

RU-A1-03-019.notes: Verbs in -овать replace -ова- with -у- in the present: рисовать → рисую, рисует. The same applies to фотографировать, путешествовать.

RU-A1-03-020.notes: мочь has a г / ж alternation: могу and могут with г, the middle forms with ж (можешь, может). It's followed by an infinitive.

RU-A1-03-021.notes: ты takes the ж form: можешь. Ты можешь…? is the everyday way to ask a favour; Не мог бы ты…? is politer.

RU-A1-03-022.notes: они returns to г: могут. Only я and они keep the г of the stem (могу, могут); the forms in between all have ж. The past tense also has г: мог, могла, могли.

RU-A1-03-023.notes: есть (eat) is irregular: ем, ешь, ест, едим, едите, едят. The ты form ешь looks like the imperative too.

RU-A1-03-024.notes: мы of есть (eat) is едим, from a stem with д: едим, едите, едят. Don't confuse with есть meaning 'there is'.

RU-A1-03-025.notes: пить keeps only the root consonant in the present: пью, пьёшь, пьют, with a soft sign before the vowel. много + genitive (воды) follows.
RU-A1-03-025.tr: I drink a lot of water.
RU-A1-03-025.flag: dup: replaced Я пью кофе (near-identical to A1-02-016 and B1-06-001)

RU-A1-03-026.notes: ты of пить is пьёшь, with stressed ё. Чай с молоком (with milk) uses the instrumental after с. The past tense keeps the full stem: пил, пила, пили.
RU-A1-03-026.tr: Do you take milk in your tea?
RU-A1-03-026.flag: dup: replaced Что ты пьёшь? (near-identical to Что ты ешь?)

RU-A1-03-027.notes: брать inserts е in the present: беру, берёшь. брать такси = take a taxi; the perfective is взять (возьму).

RU-A1-03-028.notes: давать drops -ва- in the present: даю, даёшь, даёт. The same applies to вставать (встаю) and узнавать (узнаю).

RU-A1-03-029.notes: учиться is reflexive, and after the vowel-less я form the particle is -сь: учусь. With an infinitive it means 'learn to': учусь играть.
RU-A1-03-029.tr: I'm learning to play the guitar.
RU-A1-03-029.flag: dup: replaced Я учусь в университете (same as A1-05-016)

RU-A1-03-030.notes: улица is the subject and называться is reflexive: называется (it is called). For people the verb is звать: как тебя зовут.

RU-A1-03-031.notes: заниматься takes the instrumental: заниматься спортом (do sport). The он form ends in -ется, -ся after a consonant.

RU-A1-03-032.notes: вы takes -итесь after a vowel: учитесь. Где вы учитесь? asks where someone is a student; Где вы работаете? is the equivalent for a job. The reflexive is -сь after any vowel.

RU-A1-03-033.notes: фильм starts by itself, so the reflexive начинаться: начинается. Transitive начинать needs an object: я начинаю урок.

RU-A1-04-001.notes: The cue says a man, so the past takes the masculine -л: читал. The past tense marks gender, not person: я, ты and он all use читал.

RU-A1-04-002.notes: A woman speaking takes the feminine -ла: работала. дома (at home) is an adverb, unlike домой (home, as a destination).

RU-A1-04-003.notes: мы takes the plural -ли: смотрели. The plural past is the same for all genders and persons. Вчера вечером (last night, literally yesterday evening) sets the time frame.
RU-A1-04-003.flag: dup: replaced Мы смотрели фильм (flagged against Мы смотрим фильм)

RU-A1-04-004.notes: Speaking to a man, ты takes the masculine past: был. The past of быть is the only way to say 'was'; the present has no verb at all.

RU-A1-04-005.notes: Speaking to a woman, ты takes the feminine была, with the stress on the ending (была́). The other forms, был, было and были, are stem-stressed.
RU-A1-04-005.text: (To a woman) Ты вчера {{c1::была::быть · past}} на работе?
RU-A1-04-005.flag: dup: replaced Где ты была вчера? (near-identical to A1-04-004)

RU-A1-04-006.notes: письмо is neuter, so быть takes -о: было. The past of быть agrees with the subject, which here is a thing.

RU-A1-04-007.notes: они takes -ли: жили. в Казани is prepositional; Казань is a feminine -ь noun, hence -и. The past tense needs no person ending, so the pronoun is rarely dropped.

RU-A1-04-008.notes: идти has an irregular past built on a different stem: шёл, шла, шло, шли. A woman says шла. The prefixed verbs follow it: пришёл, пришла, ушёл, ушла.

RU-A1-04-009.notes: он with идти gives шёл, with ё. The imperfective past of a single trip in progress describes the walk itself, not its completion.

RU-A1-04-010.notes: The compound future is буду + imperfective infinitive: буду работать. It describes a process or activity, with no focus on finishing.

RU-A1-04-011.notes: ты takes будешь + infinitive: будешь делать. Что ты будешь делать вечером? is the everyday question about plans.

RU-A1-04-012.notes: мы takes будем + infinitive: будем жить. в Петербурге is the prepositional of Петербург. Only imperfective verbs form this compound future; perfectives use their present forms.

RU-A1-04-013.notes: быть on its own forms a simple future: буду (I will be). Never буду быть: the infinitive isn't repeated.
RU-A1-04-013.tip: буду быть is wrong; буду alone means 'I will be'.
RU-A1-04-013.text: Я {{c1::буду::быть · future}} в офисе до шести.
RU-A1-04-013.tr: I'll be in the office until six.
RU-A1-04-013.flag: dup: replaced Завтра я буду дома (near-identical to A1-04-010)

RU-A1-04-014.notes: они takes будут: будут здесь. в пять = at five; the word часов is often dropped in speech. There's no infinitive, as быть alone gives the future of 'be'.

RU-A1-05-001.notes: в + a place takes the prepositional, and feminine -а becomes -е: Москва → в Москве. This is the default prepositional ending for most nouns.
RU-A1-05-001.flag: dup: replaced Я живу в Москве (also in A1-03-013 and A1-06-021)

RU-A1-05-002.notes: на (on a surface) + prepositional: стол → на столе. лежать is used for things lying flat, such as a book.

RU-A1-05-003.notes: банк ends in к, but the prepositional is still -е: в банке. Only ы / и are affected by the spelling rule.

RU-A1-05-004.notes: Nouns in -ия take -ии in the prepositional: Россия → в России. в Россие is a common error. The dative is also -ии (к России), and so is the genitive (из России).

RU-A1-05-005.notes: Feminine nouns in -ь take -и in the prepositional: тетрадь → в тетради. Masculine -ь nouns take -е: в словаре.

RU-A1-05-006.notes: лес is one of the masculine nouns with a stressed -у after в / на: в лесу. After о (about) it's regular: о лесе.
RU-A1-05-006.flag: dup: replaced Мы гуляем в лесу (flagged against Мы гуляем в парке)

RU-A1-05-007.notes: аэропорт takes the locative -у: в аэропорту, with stress on the ending. The form в аэропорте is heard but non-standard. After о it's regular: об аэропорте.

RU-A1-05-008.notes: о (about) + prepositional: брат → о брате. The translation adds 'my' because Russian usually omits obvious possessives.

RU-A1-05-009.notes: думать о + prepositional: мама → о маме. Feminine -а nouns take -е, so the prepositional matches the dative here (маме).

RU-A1-05-010.notes: Neuter nouns in -ие take -ии: общежитие → в общежитии. The same goes for здание (в здании) and упражнение.
RU-A1-05-010.tr: The students live in a hall of residence.
RU-A1-05-010.flag: dup: replaced Мы живём в общежитии (flagged against Мы живём в России)

RU-A1-05-011.notes: здание is neuter in -ие, so в этом здании, with the demonstrative in its own prepositional form, этом.

RU-A1-05-012.notes: Names in -ия follow the same rule: Мария → о Марии. Short names in -а (Анна) take -е: об Анне, with об before a vowel.
RU-A1-05-012.flag: dup: replaced Мы говорили о Марии (flagged against two other Мы говорили о… sentences)

RU-A1-05-013.notes: работа is one of the на nouns (на работе), while магазин takes в (в магазине). There's no rule that predicts на; it has to be learned.

RU-A1-05-014.notes: Events take на: на концерте, на уроке, на собрании. концерт is an occasion, not a building, which is why в fails. The concert hall itself would be в зале.

RU-A1-05-015.notes: улица takes на: на улице (outside, in the street). в улице is impossible. The same на appears with площадь (на площади) and проспект (на проспекте).

RU-A1-05-016.notes: Educational institutions take в: в университете, в школе. But a faculty or year group takes на: на факультете, на втором курсе.

RU-A1-05-017.notes: почта is a fixed на noun: на почте, like на вокзале and на заводе. Historically these were open spaces or services, not buildings.

RU-A1-05-018.notes: вокзал takes на: на вокзале. The perfective future встретимся makes it a plan for one occasion. Airports, by contrast, take в: в аэропорту.

RU-A1-05-019.notes: центр takes в: в центре, as for most bounded areas. на окраине (on the outskirts) is the contrasting на form.

RU-A1-05-020.notes: о + он gives о нём: the н- prefix appears on third-person pronouns after a preposition. нём has a stressed ё.
RU-A1-05-020.text: Все в классе говорят {{c1::о нём::о + он (prepositional)}}.
RU-A1-05-020.tr: Everyone in the class is talking about him.
RU-A1-05-020.flag: dup: replaced Мы говорили о нём (flagged against two other Мы говорили о… sentences)

RU-A1-05-021.notes: о + она gives о ней, again with the н- prefix. The dative and the prepositional coincide for она: ей / ней.

RU-A1-05-022.notes: о becomes обо before мне: обо мне. The other pronouns keep о (о тебе, о нас), and об is used before vowels (об этом).

RU-A1-05-023.notes: доме is masculine prepositional, so the adjective takes -ом: в новом доме. Adjectives have their own prepositional endings, distinct from nouns.

RU-A1-05-024.notes: комнате is feminine prepositional, so the adjective takes -ой: в красивой комнате. The feminine -ой covers genitive, dative, instrumental and prepositional.

RU-A1-05-025.notes: вторник begins with в + another consonant, so в becomes во: во вторник. в среду and в четверг keep plain в.

RU-A1-05-026.notes: к becomes ко before мне: ко мне. The extra vowel prevents an awkward cluster; к тебе, к нему stay plain.

RU-A1-05-027.notes: стол begins with с + consonant, so с becomes со: со стола. с + genitive here means 'off, down from'.

RU-A1-05-028.notes: Франции begins with ф, which with в forms a hard cluster, so во Франции. в Финляндии, by contrast, keeps в.

RU-A1-06-001.notes: The direct object of купить is accusative, and feminine -а becomes -у: книгу. The demonstrative also agrees: эту.
RU-A1-06-001.text: (To a man) Где ты купил эту {{c1::книгу::книга · accusative}}?
RU-A1-06-001.tr: Where did you buy this book?
RU-A1-06-001.flag: dup: replaced Я читаю книгу (same as A1-03-001)

RU-A1-06-002.notes: вода is the object of пить, so -а → -у: воду. With пить, the stress in this form falls on the stem: вóду.

RU-A1-06-003.notes: музыка becomes музыку as the object of любить. The accusative feminine is the only singular case where -а gives -у.

RU-A1-06-004.notes: ждать takes the accusative for specific people: ждать маму. With abstract things it often takes the genitive instead: ждать ответа.

RU-A1-06-005.notes: история is feminine in -ия, so -ю: историю. изучать means study a subject in depth and always takes an object.

RU-A1-06-006.notes: стол is masculine and inanimate, so its accusative looks the same as the nominative. Only animate masculine nouns change (брата).

RU-A1-06-007.notes: брат is animate, so the accusative takes the genitive form: брата. встречать (meet, at a station) takes the accusative.
RU-A1-06-007.tr: We're meeting my brother at the station.
RU-A1-06-007.flag: dup: replaced Я знаю брата (flagged against Я знаю вашего брата; translation had added 'his')

RU-A1-06-008.notes: учитель is animate and ends in -ь, so the accusative is -я: учителя. The animacy rule covers all male people and animals.

RU-A1-06-009.notes: Иван is animate, so the accusative is Ивана. Even names follow the animacy rule: Я вижу Ивана, but Я вижу стол. A woman's name in -а simply takes -у: Я вижу Анну.

RU-A1-06-010.notes: сын is animate, so сына. Animate feminine nouns don't follow this rule: they take -у / -ю (маму), and -ь nouns like дочь stay unchanged.

RU-A1-06-011.notes: я in the accusative is меня, and pronoun objects usually come before the verb in neutral speech: Ты меня понимаешь?

RU-A1-06-012.notes: ты in the accusative is тебя. Я тебя люблю is the default order; Я люблю тебя puts more weight on тебя.

RU-A1-06-013.notes: они in the accusative is их. Without a preposition there's no н- prefix; with one it becomes них (про них).

RU-A1-06-014.notes: он in the accusative is его, pronounced with в (yevó). It looks like the possessive his, but here it's the object.

RU-A1-06-015.notes: Как вас зовут? literally 'how do they call you': вас is the accusative object of the plural verb зовут. It's the standard polite way to ask a name.

RU-A1-06-016.notes: The cue says a man is speaking, and тебя is the accusative object of узнал. Pronoun objects normally precede the verb.
RU-A1-06-016.text: (A man speaking) Я {{c1::тебя::ты · accusative}} сразу узнал.
RU-A1-06-016.flag: dup: replaced Как тебя зовут? (same frame as A1-06-015 Как вас зовут?)

RU-A1-06-017.notes: машину is feminine accusative, so the adjective takes -ую: новую. Feminine accusative is the only adjective case with -ую.

RU-A1-06-018.notes: книгу is feminine accusative, so the adjective is интересную. Adjective and noun share the -у of the accusative. The masculine counterpart would be интересный фильм, unchanged.

RU-A1-06-019.notes: брата is animate masculine accusative, so the possessive takes the genitive form: вашего. Inanimate nouns would keep ваш.

RU-A1-06-020.notes: живёшь describes location, so где; идёшь describes direction, so куда. English 'where' covers both. The third member, откуда, asks for the starting point.

RU-A1-06-021.notes: Location (живу) takes в + prepositional, Москве; direction (еду) takes в + accusative, Москву. The preposition is the same; the case carries the difference.

RU-A1-06-022.notes: Going somewhere is direction, so на + accusative: на работу. The location counterpart is на работе. на-nouns keep на for both; only the case shifts.

RU-A1-06-023.notes: Being at work is location, so на + prepositional: на работе. Сейчас я на работе has no verb, as the present of быть is omitted.

RU-A1-06-024.notes: идём is direction, so в + accusative: в школу. The prepositional в школе would mean 'at school'. Feminine -а nouns make the contrast visible: -у versus -е.

RU-A1-07-001.notes: Possession uses у + genitive + есть: у меня есть. меня here is the genitive of я, identical in form to the accusative.

RU-A1-07-002.notes: у + тебя (genitive of ты) + есть asks whether someone has something. есть can be dropped when the focus is the thing itself: У тебя машина?

RU-A1-07-003.notes: After у, он becomes него with the н- prefix: у него. Without a preposition it's его (Его нет дома). The same н- appears in у неё and у них.

RU-A1-07-004.notes: у + нас (genitive of мы). время is a neuter noun in -мя, and here it's the subject of есть. In the negative it would become genitive: У нас нет времени.

RU-A1-07-005.notes: Possession with a noun owner also uses у + genitive: сестра → у сестры. The two cats follow in the genitive singular after две.

RU-A1-07-006.notes: нет + genitive denies possession: брат → брата. In the negative, есть disappears and the thing owned goes into the genitive.

RU-A1-07-007.notes: время is irregular: the genitive is времени, with -ен-. Other -мя nouns (имя, знамя) behave the same way. нет + genitive is required, so время alone is impossible here.

RU-A1-07-008.notes: нет + genitive also states absence: вода → воды. Здесь нет is 'there's no… here', with no possessor.

RU-A1-07-009.notes: машина is feminine, so the genitive is -ы: машины. у неё uses the н- form of её after the preposition.

RU-A1-07-010.notes: урок is masculine, so -а: урока. Сегодня нет урока = there's no lesson today; the past would be не было урока.

RU-A1-07-011.notes: ложка has a к stem, so the feminine genitive is spelt -и, not -ы: ложки. The spelling rule applies in every case.
RU-A1-07-011.tr: There isn't a spoon on the table.
RU-A1-07-011.flag: dup: replaced У меня нет книги (one of four У меня нет… sentences); answer книги → ложки

RU-A1-07-012.notes: Absence of a person also uses нет + genitive: его нет дома. Without the preposition there's no н-: его, not него.

RU-A1-07-013.notes: не negates a word (не знаю); нет is the answer 'no' and also the verb of absence. Нет, спасибо declines an offer.

RU-A1-07-014.notes: Absence takes нет + genitive (молока). не would need a verb to negate. The past is не было молока and the future не будет молока, with the verb in the neuter.
RU-A1-07-014.tr: There's no milk in the fridge.
RU-A1-07-014.flag: dup: replaced У меня нет машины (one of four У меня нет… sentences)

RU-A1-07-015.notes: The owner follows the thing in the genitive: дом мамы. In speech, possessive adjectives such as мамин дом are more common (B2).

RU-A1-07-016.notes: Анна → Анны in the genitive. The possessor comes after: сумка Анны, the reverse of English 'Anna's bag'.

RU-A1-07-017.notes: город takes -а in the genitive: центр города. This 'of' genitive is the commonest use of the case. The possessor always follows: центр города, never города центр.

RU-A1-07-018.notes: папа is masculine but declines like a feminine -а noun: папы. Gender affects agreement; declension follows the ending.

RU-A1-07-019.notes: After два, the noun takes the genitive singular: сын → сына. Despite the form, the meaning is plural.
RU-A1-07-019.tr: There are two sons in the family.
RU-A1-07-019.flag: dup: replaced У меня два брата (flagged against У меня нет брата); answer брата → сына

RU-A1-07-020.notes: Compound numbers follow their last digit: двадцать два → года (genitive singular). Age uses the dative of the person: мне.

RU-A1-07-021.notes: Numbers from 5 up take the genitive plural, and год has the suppletive form лет: тридцать лет. годов exists but means 'years' as decades or periods.

RU-A1-07-022.notes: три takes the genitive singular: часа. Сейчас три часа = it's three o'clock; the verb is omitted in the present.

RU-A1-07-023.notes: пять takes the genitive plural: часов. The ending -ов is the masculine hard default. From пять to двадцать every number takes the genitive plural.

RU-A1-07-024.notes: сто (100) takes the genitive plural, and рубль ends in -ь, so -ей: рублей. стоить + amount = cost. With 1, 2 or 3 it would be рубль, рубля, рубля.

RU-A1-07-025.notes: три takes the genitive singular, сестры; the stress moves to the ending (сестры́). Five sisters would be пять сестёр.

RU-A1-08-001.notes: нравиться makes the thing liked the subject and the person the dative: мне нравится. Literally 'this music pleases me'.

RU-A1-08-002.notes: ты in the dative is тебе, the experiencer of нравится. The verb is singular because Москва is singular.

RU-A1-08-003.notes: Age uses the dative of the person: ему двадцать лет. он in the dative is ему, with no н- since there's no preposition.

RU-A1-08-004.notes: надо + infinitive takes the person in the dative: нам надо идти. The sentence has no grammatical subject.

RU-A1-08-005.notes: Feelings and sensations take dative + adverb: ей холодно. Она холодная would describe her character (cold), not how she feels. The same pattern gives мне жарко, нам скучно.

RU-A1-08-006.notes: нужна agrees with помощь (feminine), and the person in need is in the dative: вам. Вам нужна помощь? is a standard offer.

RU-A1-08-007.notes: город is singular, so нравится; цветы is plural, so нравятся. The verb agrees with the thing liked, not with мне.

RU-A1-08-008.notes: An infinitive as the thing liked takes the singular нравится. Ему нравится читать = he likes reading.

RU-A1-08-009.notes: звонить takes the dative of the person called: маме. It's 'ring to someone', unlike the English direct object.

RU-A1-08-010.notes: The recipient of a letter is in the dative: брату. The letter itself, письмо, is the accusative object.

RU-A1-08-011.notes: к + dative means going to a person: к врачу (to the doctor's). The ending -у marks the masculine dative.

RU-A1-08-012.notes: подарить takes the recipient in the dative: Анне. Feminine -а nouns take -е in the dative. The gift itself is the accusative object, as with дать and показать.

RU-A1-08-013.notes: помогать takes the dative, not the accusative: помогать соседу. English 'help someone' misleads learners into the accusative.
RU-A1-08-013.flag: dup: replaced Мы помогаем другу (near-identical to B1 Мы помогаем друг другу); answer другу → соседу

RU-A1-08-014.notes: другу is a person, so going to their place takes к + dative. в + accusative is for places: в школу, в магазин.
RU-A1-08-014.tip: к for people, в / на for places.

RU-A1-08-015.notes: с (with) + instrumental: брат → с братом. The masculine instrumental ending is -ом. Soft masculine nouns take -ем instead: с учителем, с Игорем.

RU-A1-08-016.notes: с + instrumental: мама → с мамой. Feminine -а nouns take -ой, soft -я nouns take -ей (с Таней). With a mother, Russian often says мы с мамой, meaning 'Mum and I'.

RU-A1-08-017.notes: с + instrumental also marks what something comes with: чай с сахаром. без + genitive is the opposite: без сахара.

RU-A1-08-018.notes: с becomes со before мной: со мной. Пойдём со мной! is an invitation using the perfective future мы form.

RU-A1-08-019.notes: с + ты gives с тобой. поговорить с кем = talk to someone; Russian uses 'with' where English uses 'to'.

RU-A1-08-020.notes: с + она gives с ней (also с нею, literary). The н- prefix appears because of the preposition. Without a preposition the instrumental is ей: Я горжусь ей.

RU-A1-08-021.notes: заниматься takes the instrumental without a preposition: заниматься музыкой. It's the usual verb for hobbies and sports.

RU-A1-08-022.notes: учитель ends in -ь, so the instrumental is -ем: с учителем. говорить с = talk to. The plural is учителя, with stressed -я, so с учителями.

RU-A1-09-001.notes: Right now, in one direction → идти (иду); every day, a habit → ходить (хожу). Both mean 'go on foot'. ходить changes д → ж in the я form only.

RU-A1-09-002.notes: By transport, one direction now → ехать (еду); a regular trip → ездить (ездим). The verb pair changes with the means of travel.

RU-A1-09-003.notes: A round trip in the past (went and came back) uses the multidirectional ходил. шёл would mean he was on his way.

RU-A1-09-004.notes: на поезде means travelling by transport, so ехать, not идти. Russians never use идти for a journey by vehicle, though a train or bus itself идёт.

RU-A1-09-005.notes: One direction now → идти: идёшь. домой is the adverb of direction (home); дома means 'at home'. Mixing them (иду дома) is a classic learner error.

RU-A1-09-006.notes: Means of transport take на + prepositional: на автобусе, на метро. A habit uses ездить: я езжу, with д → ж in the я form. A single trip would be еду.

RU-A1-09-007.notes: People take their own prepositions: у + genitive (at someone's), к + dative (to them), от + genitive (from them). Places use в / на / из / с instead.
RU-A1-09-007.text:
(A man speaking) Я был {{c1::у врача::at the doctor's (у + genitive)}}.
Я иду {{c2::к врачу::to the doctor's (к + dative)}}.
Я иду {{c3::от врача::from the doctor's (от + genitive)}}.
RU-A1-09-007.flag: text: added (A man speaking), as был needs the speaker's gender

RU-A1-09-008.notes: и simply adds; а contrasts two parallel facts (I… whereas my brother…); но marks something unexpected or contrary. English 'and' covers both и and many uses of а.

RU-A1-09-009.notes: After a negated element, the correction takes а: не чай, а кофе. но here would be wrong. The pattern не X, а Y is the standard way to say 'not X but Y'.

RU-A1-09-010.notes: потому что introduces the reason (I'm ill); поэтому introduces the result (I'm at home). The order of clauses flips with the word.

RU-A1-09-011.notes: Asking for origin takes откуда (from where). Откуда вы? needs no verb, since the present of быть is dropped. The answer uses из + genitive: Я из Англии.

RU-A1-09-012.notes: Price questions use сколько + стоит. сколько also takes the genitive: сколько денег, сколько времени.

RU-A1-09-013.notes: почему asks for a cause; зачем asks for a purpose (what for). Почему ты не спишь? = why aren't you asleep?

RU-A1-09-014.notes: когда asks for a time and usually comes first; the verb often precedes the subject in such questions: начинается урок.
